title: Canon Correction
description: ONE out-of-band, adjudicated correction to an ALREADY-FROZEN canon.json entries{} record, submitted to canon_validate.py --correct as a whole JSON document and appended verbatim to canon.json's corrections[] once applied (#495). The same shape is both the request and the record, deliberately: two shapes for one decision drift apart, and the record's whole job is to let the next operator see what was adjudicated. This is NOT a relaxed merge -- an ordinary --merge-batches item carrying a differing resolution for a frozen source_form still collides and still raises; correction is a separate, explicitly-named route. old_entry is a REQUIRED interlock, not documentation: --correct refuses, naming both values, when it does not equal what is on disk, so the mode cannot be used blind against a canon.json that moved since it was read. disposition:"correct" replaces the record under the same source_form key (new_entry required, and its own source_form field must equal that key); disposition:"remove" deletes it (new_entry forbidden) -- removal is the sanctioned repair for an entry that should never have existed, and the only route to clear canon_adjudication_audit.py's BLOCKING collapsed_split, which no substituted bare entry can satisfy. A key RENAME is a remove followed by an ordinary --merge-batches under the new key, never a third disposition.

source_form.description: The entries{} key being corrected. Must already be present -- a correction never inserts blind; adding a new name is --merge-batches' job.

old_entry.description: The value the caller states is CURRENTLY on disk under source_form. The blind-use interlock: --correct refuses, naming both, when this does not match. Deliberately a plain object rather than a $ref to canon-entry.schema.json, and the asymmetry with new_entry is the point -- old_entry's job is EQUALITY against what is on disk, not shape, and the entry most in need of correcting is the one that fails its own schema. A hand-edited canon.json (the only repair route that existed before this mode) can hold exactly that, and --validate-only exists to find it; requiring the old value to validate would leave those entries with no route at all, which is the defect this mode closes. new_entry IS $ref-validated, because it becomes the frozen record.

new_entry.description: The corrected record. Required for disposition:"correct", forbidden for disposition:"remove".

reason.description: Why this frozen decision was wrong, in the corrector's own words. Required and non-blank -- an unexplained diff is the thing #495 exists to stop -- but deliberately NOT length-capped: canon-entry.schema.json's own `note` is unbounded and rides in the same document via new_entry, so a cap here would bound one field while leaving the record's total size exactly as open as every other operator-authored free text in canon.json. Same convention as `note`, no special pleading.
